subject: Confirming demo -> technical throughput sizing call for Quantipay
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia@quantipay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps and scheduling: demo -> throughput sizing call for Quantipay

Hi Amelia — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock in a dedicated capacity sizing session (technical deep dive focused on throughput / latency):

Recap (brief):
- Goal: quantify GPU footprint and latency SLOs for Quantipay's real-time fraud scoring (mixed synchronous inference + batched bulk scoring).
- Important constraints you mentioned: 99th-pct latency target ~150ms for synchr. API, peak QPS bursts up to ~4k for short windows, average seq len ~512 tokens for prompts + context.

Proposed next step: a 60–75 minute technical throughput/latency sizing call where we pair your infra/eng with our Solutions Eng to map workload -> recommended pool config (GPU type, pool size, burst policy).

I have the following windows (PDT) — please pick one or suggest alternatives:
- Thu 19 Jun, 10:00–11:15
- Thu 19 Jun, 15:00–16:15
- Fri 20 Jun, 08:30–09:45

Prep asks (to make the call productive):
- A small sample of your real request profile (CSV or traffic snapshot): per-minute QPS, percentile seq lengths, and % streaming vs non-streaming over a 24–72h window.
- Current concurrency / retry behaviour and any existing batching in the client.
- Any compliance constraints (data residency/retention) we should be aware of for a Private/Dedicated deployment.

I've attached our short discovery notes from today's call for reference (discovery_notes_quantipay.pdf). Ben (copied) will join the sizing call as SE.

If you confirm a slot I’ll send a calendar invite with a Zoom link and a brief agenda.

Thanks — Neha

-- 
Neha Kapoor | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference for engineering teams

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 17:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Next steps and scheduling: demo -> throughput sizing call for Quantipay

Neha — thanks for the clear summary and for capturing the asks. Friday morning (your Fri 08:30 PDT) would work best for our engs. Can we lock Fri 20 Jun, 08:30–09:30 PDT? I’ll confirm with Daniel (CTO) and our infra lead on the sample data.

Couple quick notes:
- We can provide a 48h traffic dump with per-minute QPS and token counts — will that be enough?
- We’d like Ben on the call to help validate quantization/precision tradeoffs — thanks for looping him in.

Once confirmed I’ll add procurement on the invite for a short intro to licensing questions.

Best,
Amelia

Ben — can you own the technical checklist / run through the throughput template and confirm any extra artifacts you want before the call? I attached a mutual action plan draft we usually use for sizing + procurement context (mutual_action_plan_qpay.docx).

Amelia / Daniel / procurement — for the traffic snapshot, the 48h per-minute QPS + percentile token lengths is ideal. If you can include a short example of a typical request payload (anonymized), that will speed up our initial mapping.

1) 10–15m — short context & objectives (Quantipay infra + Redwood SE)
2) 30–40m — workload profile walkthrough, live QPS/latency analysis, model variant and quantization options
3) 10–15m — recommended pool config, autoscaling/burst settings, follow-ups (MVP vs long-term)

I’ll add a HubSpot link to the deal in the invite so procurement has visibility.

Thanks,
Neha

Subject: Calendar invite + prep for Friday's sizing call (Quantipay)

Hi all — I just sent the calendar invite for Fri 20 Jun, 08:30–09:30 PDT (Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/987654321). Quick prep checklist so we hit the ground running:

Before the call (please upload to the shared link or reply to this thread):
- 48h per-minute QPS CSV (columns: timestamp, requests_per_minute, median_tokens, p90_tokens, p99_tokens) — see attached throughput_template.csv for format.
- Example anonymized request + response (one or two examples).
- Any peak day/week schedules and known blackout windows.

On the call I’ll validate expected KV cache reuse, batching opportunities, and latency budgets. If you have an internal engineer who can share short-term load shaping plans that will help us size burst capacity correctly.

Looking forward — Ben
